'''Justyna Wydrzyńska''' is a Polish [[Abortion-rights movement|abortion-rights]] activist. She is the first abortion-rights activist in Europe to be convicted of aiding a woman to get an abortion.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Grant |first=Rebecca |date=2023-06-23 |title=The Conviction of Justyna Wydrzyńska |language=en-US |url=https://www.thenation.com/?post_type=article&p=448142 |access-date=2023-10-21 |issn=0027-8378}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Strzyżyńska |first=Weronika |date=2022-03-28 |title=Polish woman is first activist to face trial for violating strict abortion law |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2022/mar/28/polish-woman-is-first-to-face-trial-for-violating-strict-abortion-law |access-date=2023-10-21 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lott-Lavigna |first=Ruby |date=2022-06-16 |title=She Sent a Woman Abortion Pills. Now She Faces 3 Years in Prison. |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/poland-abortion-justyna-wydrzynska/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Vice |language=en}}</ref>

== Activism ==
Wydrzyńska launched Kobiety w Sieci, an online website providing information about self-induced medical abortions, after she had her own induced abortion in 2006.<ref name=":0" /> 

In 2016, Wydrzyńska and three other women founded the [[Abortion Dream Team]].<ref name=":0" />

In December 2019, Wydrzyńska helped found Abortion Without Borders, an initiative connecting Polish women with abortion providers in Germany, Czech Republic, Austria, the Netherlands, and the UK.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2020-12-07 |title=Inside the fight against Poland's abortion ban |url=https://www.huckmag.com/article/inside-the-fight-against-polands-abortion-ban |access-date=2023-11-05 |website=Huck |language=en}}</ref><ref>https://abortion.eu/#about</ref>

In 2023, Wydrzyńska was shortlisted, alongside two other abortion rights activists, for the [[Sakharov Prize|Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ray |first=Nat |date=2023-10-12 |title=Abortion Rights Defenders Shortlisted for European Parliament Prize for Freedom of Thought |url=https://reproductiverights.org/abortion-rights-defenders-nominated-european-parliament-sakharov-prize/ |access-date=2023-11-05 |website=Center for Reproductive Rights |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Arrest and trial ==
[[File:Ani jednej wiecej 2023 - Justyna Wydrzynska and Kiwi.jpg|thumb|Justyna Wydrzyńska in 2023.]]
In November 2021, Wydrzyńska was arrested after sending abortion pills to a pregnant woman through the mail in 2020.<ref name=":0" /> She was charged with "intent to aid an abortion and unauthorized distribution of a pharmaceutical".<ref name=":0" /> Wydrzyńska's defense argued that she had sent the abortion pills, but that doing so was "an act of human rights", that she had not aided an abortion, since the pregnant woman had not ended up taking the pills, and that the law against aiding an abortion, as written, should not apply to Wydrzyńska or other similar activists.<ref name=":0" />

Her first court date was in August 2022.<ref name=":0" /> Representatives from human rights groups and European embassies were denied entry to the proceedings.<ref name=":0" /> An ultraconservative, catholic organization Ordo Iuris was allowed entry to the proceedings as legal representatives of the foetus.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-08 |title=Aktywistka przed sądem za pomoc w aborcji. A Ordo Iuris chce reprezentować nienarodzony płód|url=https://www.wysokieobcasy.pl/wysokie-obcasy/7,182090,28316330,justyna-wydrzynska-przed-sadem-za-pomoc-w-aborcji-a-ordo-iuris.html?disableRedirects=true|access-date=2025-04-08 |website=Wysokie Obcasy|language=pl}}</ref>

In March 2023, Wydrzyńska was convicted with abetting an abortion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-24 |title=Guilty of abetting abortion, Polish woman vows to fight on |url=https://apnews.com/article/poland-abortion-rights-activist-court-justice-eu-4510931835c2d950ca73535657267d41 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Niamh |date=2023-03-15 |title=Polish court convicts rights activist for supplying pregnant woman with abortion pills |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/15/europe/poland-abortion-activist-justyna-wydrzyska-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> She was sentenced to 8 months of community service.<ref name=":1" /> Her charges and conviction were condemned by [[Amnesty International]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-14 |title=Conviction of Polish abortion activist 'chilling' |url=https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/03/poland-conviction-of-activist-prosecuted-for-aiding-an-abortion-offers-chilling-snapshot-of-future/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Amnesty International |language=en}}</ref> [[Human Rights Watch]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-13 |title=Poland: End Prosecution of Abortion Activist |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/07/13/poland-end-prosecution-abortion-activist |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Human Rights Watch |language=en}}</ref> the [[International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=FIGO urges Polish authorities to drop all charges against Justyna Wydrzyńska |url=https://www.figo.org/news/figo-urges-polish-authorities-drop-all-charges-against-justyna-wydrzynska |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=[[International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics]] |language=en}}</ref> the [[International Planned Parenthood Federation]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-14 |title=Poland: IPPF EN is appalled by the guilty verdict in the case of Justyna Wydrzyńska |url=https://europe.ippf.org/media-center/poland-ippf-en-appalled-guilty-verdict-case-justyna-wydrzynska |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=IPPF Europe & Central Asia |language=en}}</ref> and the [[United Nations]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2023 |title=UN experts urge Poland to acquit woman human rights defender Justyna Wydrzyńska |url=https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2023/03/un-experts-urge-poland-acquit-woman-human-rights-defender-justyna-wydrzynska|website=[[OHCHR]]}}</ref>

In February 2025, the Warsaw Court of Appeals overturned Wydrzyńska's conviction and ordered she be given a retrial, citing concerns of judicial independence in the original trial.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2025-02-13 |title=Polish court orders retrial of woman found guilty of helping terminate pregnancy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/feb/13/polish-court-orders-retrial-of-woman-found-guilty-of-helping-terminate-pregnancy |access-date=2026-02-18 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Berro Pizzarossa |first=Lucía |last2=Jelinska |first2=Kinga |last3=Broniarczyk |first3=Natalia |author-link3=Natalia Broniarczyk |date=2025-06-04 |title=Solidarity on Trial: The Criminalization of Abortion Activism in Poland |url=https://petrieflom.law.harvard.edu/2025/06/04/solidarity-on-trial-the-criminalization-of-abortion-activism-in-poland/ |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=Petrie-Flom Center |publisher=[[Harvard University]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wydrzyńska was initially a chemist.<ref name=":0" />

As of 2020, she was living in the Polish town of [[Przasnysz]].<ref name=":2" />
